issues.legal_issue: A person lawfully cultivating agricultural land under a lease granted by a life-estate holder with authority to manage the land is a deemed tenant and may acquire ownership under a statutory tenant-purchase scheme.
material_facts: The landholder held a life estate and was authorized to manage the estate after attaining majority.
The settlement deed contained no specific restriction preventing the landholder from leasing the land.
The landholder leased the agricultural land to the cultivators, who lawfully cultivated it and did not fall within any of the statutory exceptions to deemed tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The cultivators were deemed tenants under section 4 and were eligible to acquire ownership under the statutory purchase scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948 deems a person lawfully cultivating another's land to be a tenant unless the person falls within an enumerated exception. Sections 32 and 32G provide for the tenant's statutory purchase and determination of price. Following Dahyalal v. Rasul Mohammed Abdul Rahim, a person lawfully cultivating land under authority derived from someone other than the owner may qualify; the exclusion of a mortgagee in possession does not necessarily exclude a cultivator inducted by that mortgagee. Prabhu v. Ramdeo and section 76(a) of the Transfer of Property Act support the possibility that statutory tenancy protections may attach to a person inducted by a mortgagee in possession.

predicates.statutory_tenant_purchase_proceeding: A proceeding concerned whether an agricultural cultivator qualified for ownership through a statutory tenant-purchase scheme.
predicates.land_belonged_to_another: The agricultural land belonged to someone other than the person cultivating it.
predicates.cultivator_lawfully_cultivated_land: The person cultivated the land under lawful authority.
predicates.cultivator_not_in_excluded_category: The cultivator was not a family member, qualifying servant or labourer, or mortgagee in possession within the statutory exceptions.
predicates.life_estate_holder_authorized_to_manage: A person holding a life estate had authority to manage the land.
predicates.life_estate_holder_leased_land: The life-estate holder granted the cultivator a lease of the land.

issues.definition: When a statutory tenant-purchase proceeding concerns land belonging to another, and a person lawfully cultivates it under a lease granted by a life-estate holder authorized to manage it, the person qualifies if not within an excluded category.

issues.legal_issue: A remainder that takes effect only upon the life-estate holder's death is contingent during the holder's lifetime and does not make the remainder-holders present owners for purposes of postponing statutory purchase because they are minors.
material_facts: The settlement gave the landholder a life interest and provided for the property to pass to children living at the landholder's death.
The children had no right to the property during the landholder's lifetime.
The appellant argued that the children's minority postponed the statutory purchase date.
issues.conclusion: The landholder held a vested interest during her lifetime, while the children's interests were contingent; the children's minority did not postpone the statutory purchase.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13 of the Transfer of Property Act requires a prior interest where property is transferred for the benefit of an unborn person. The court construed the settlement as giving the life-estate holder a present vested interest and the children an interest contingent on her death. Under section 32F of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, postponement based on a landlord's minority did not apply on the asserted basis that the children were present owners. Rajes Kanta Roy v. Santi Debi was distinguished; the court applied the principles concerning vested and contingent interests by construing the settlement as a whole.

predicates.statutory_tenant_purchase_proceeding: A proceeding concerned whether an agricultural cultivator qualified for ownership through a statutory tenant-purchase scheme.
predicates.life_estate_holder_has_present_vested_in: The settlement gave the life-estate holder a present interest in the property during her lifetime.
predicates.remainder_effective_only_on_life_estate_: The remainder-holders could receive an interest in the property only when the life estate ended.
predicates.remaindermen_are_minors: The persons entitled to the remainder were minors when postponement of purchase was claimed.

issues.definition: Where a tenant-purchase proceeding concerns property in which the life-estate holder has a present vested interest and the remainder takes effect only when that estate ends, the remaindermen's minority does not postpone statutory purchase.

issues.legal_issue: A general restriction on encumbering property does not prevent a life-estate holder authorized to manage it from leasing agricultural land when the settlement expresses no contrary intention.
material_facts: The settlement authorized the life-estate holder to manage the estate after attaining majority.
The settlement restricted her from disposing of the property or encumbering it but did not specifically prohibit leases.
The life-estate holder leased the agricultural land as part of managing the estate.
issues.conclusion: The management authority included the right to lease the land, and the general restriction on encumbering the property did not bar the leases.
issues.legal_principle: On construction of the settlement as a whole, authority to manage or administer agricultural land as a prudent person ordinarily includes authority to lease it unless a contrary intention is expressed. A limited owner or life-estate holder may lease agricultural land during the life estate absent a clear restriction to the contrary. The court did not need to decide whether a lease would otherwise fall within the meaning of an encumbrance.

predicates.life_estate_management_dispute: The dispute concerned whether a life-estate holder's authority to manage property included authority to lease it.
predicates.life_estate_holder_authorized_to_manage: The settlement authorized the life-estate holder to manage the property.
predicates.no_specific_bar_on_leasing: The settlement did not specifically prohibit the life-estate holder from leasing the property.
predicates.life_estate_holder_leased_land: The life-estate holder granted a lease of the land.

issues.definition: When a life-estate holder is authorized to manage land and the settlement contains no specific bar on leasing, that management authority permits a lease.
